new_findings.title: An old action refresh can cancel the new slot read; returning to a slot also revives stale exportability
new_findings.scenario: Start selection/export for slot A, edit the still-enabled slot controls to B while the action is pending. The B effect starts a read. When A finishes, its captured slotStatus.refresh aborts that read and starts an A read. The A result cannot match rendered key B; no dependency changes to trigger another B read, so B is stranded loading. Separately, after a successful A read, switching A->B->A reuses the cached A result and reports idle/exportable while the new A request is pending; a now-invalid selection/download is exposed until it settles. Server checks still protect export/download authority.
new_findings.proof: Two passing temporary Vitest probes extracted the exact current useSlotStatus hook to /tmp/m10-delta-review-probe/hook.ts without editing repository source. They assert that the B signal is aborted with no live B replacement and the hook stays loading; and that A->B->A exposes old exportable=true with state idle during an unresolved fresh A request. These are controlled hook probes, not a browser E2E test.
new_findings.fix: Bind refresh ownership and settled results to the current scope and request generation. An old action completion must not abort the active slot read; either ignore it or refresh the active slot through a current-scope owner. Invalidate settled authority on scope transitions and explicitly track pending refreshes. Add deferred-response page tests covering edits during both successful and refused actions.

new_findings.title: The rebuilt parity PASS is bound to an older integrated HEAD and cannot satisfy the current gate
new_findings.scenario: Both reports still name 07e69875ccf97f5013a0095b11eb49d862846575, while 2e3997b74 subsequently changes package_export.py, including the _resolve/_require_current signatures and their call sites. Evaluating each report against requested HEAD 9c385bf9411144580b010d0b874874c8f8e9988b returns BLOCKED. Historical PASS must not be promoted to current pre-seal acceptance.
new_findings.proof: Fresh Python invocation of evaluate_quality_parity for both reports returned BLOCKED at the requested SHA. AST comparisons confirmed plan_export, snapshot_assets, metadata_document, builder_identity_digest, worker_file_digests and _build_and_publish are unchanged since the report pin; both worker files and the parity test file are byte-identical. Thus the historical measurements remain relevant to their bounded measured surface, and this is not evidence of a builder regression. It still fails the exact-HEAD contract, and this review could not refresh confined performance evidence.
new_findings.fix: Rerun the affected focused evidence in a working PostgreSQL/confinement environment, regenerate reports against a concrete reviewed code HEAD, and bind acceptance explicitly to that snapshot. Do not simply replace the SHA without documenting unchanged measured dependencies and fresh evidence for the changed export call surface.

new_findings.title: A selection change during the slot read returns the old selection as the current slot
new_findings.scenario: GET reads S1/version1 without locks and loads its receipts. Before _require_current obtains the packaging head lock, another transaction commits S2/version2. The locked check sees S2 and raises StaleHeadError, but the catch returns S1/version1/its receipts with exportable=false instead of rereading S2. The UI labels this old selection Current selection and disables export even if S2 is READY. A refresh after an action can therefore settle on an obsolete projection until another user action. A concurrent disposition change correctly withholds tokens, but a concurrent selection replacement is not returned as the new slot state.
new_findings.proof: Direct source interleaving: current_head at 814 precedes the lock/recheck at 960; the StaleHeadError branch at 842 returns the originally captured version/selection/receipts. No PostgreSQL interleaving was executable in this sandbox. This is a projection/liveness defect; the refusal does not grant stale export/download authority.
new_findings.fix: On a packaging-head change, retry the complete projection using the replacement selection and receipts, with a bounded retry/refusal policy. Preserve the masters->profile->run->disposition->packaging->grants order; taking the packaging lock first would introduce an order inversion. Add a deterministic PostgreSQL writer/read interleaving test.

locks.assessment: Read-only means no domain rows are mutated; it does not mean lock-free. _require_current acquires sorted master locks, profile/run/disposition FOR SHARE, an exclusive transaction advisory packaging lock plus head FOR SHARE, and readiness_in/load_run_observations acquires sorted grant-head FOR UPDATE. These can block publication, seal, disposition, selection and grant writers, and serialize reads on the same slot until transaction completion. Filesystem/readiness/grant checks occur while locks are held. No new order inversion/deadlock was identified in the inspected path relative to selection/export/disposition/run ordering. Runtime contention/deadlock freedom is not established because PostgreSQL was unavailable.

token_safety.assessment: New route derives user/project from authentication/path, lists scoped digest/cache-verified receipts and only issues tokens for exportable status plus an interactive Human token. Agent reads get null tokens. Locks are released before token issuance, so a writer can supersede readiness immediately afterwards; download independently snapshots/verifies bytes and reruns _require_current, which preserves safety. No new token authority bypass confirmed. Dynamic router/token verification was blocked at DB setup.
